hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 is always zero, so adding a conv on edge 1->3 cannot contribute and its usual large gain vanishes.
Edge 1->2 only carries node 1's signal, which is zero when edge 0 is none, so the conv adds nothing.
When edge 2->3 is none node 2 never reaches the output, so a conv into node 2 is wasted.
Node 2 is disconnected from the output when edge 5 is none, nullifying any op placed on edge 1->2.
Without the 1->3 edge, node 1's features reach the output only indirectly via node 2, shrinking the benefit of a conv on edge 0->1.
Removing edge 1->3 is harmless when node 1 is already dead, whereas it normally removes a useful path.
Deleting edge 0->2 costs nothing when node 2 is cut off from the output, unlike the usual case.
Removing a 3x3 conv from edge 2->3 destroys more capacity than removing a weaker op like skip, pool, or none.
Replacing a missing direct input->output edge with a 3x3 conv adds both a path and capacity, giving a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
With edge 2->3 already absent, removing the direct 0->3 edge leaves only one path into the output and causes an outsized accuracy drop.
